title: In Epistolam Beati Pauli Ad Philemonem
author: Ambrose

passages.original: (Vers. 17.) Si ergo C habes me sociam, assume illum sicut me. Tantum sc affectum habere circa Onesimum ostendit, ut tunc Philemonem, quem superius lau- dat, participem suum dicat, si istum sic susceperit, sicut Apostolum. Hoc est enim quod dixit Salomon : Serto sapienti liberi servient (Eccles. x, 28). Quod dictum terrori est Philemoni, ut saltem vel bac causa assumeret eum, si charitate flecti non posset.
passages.english: (Verse 17.) If, then, you hold me as a partner, receive him as [you would] me. He shows that he has such affection for Onesimus that he calls Philemon, whom he praised above, his partner only on condition that he receives this man just as [he would] the Apostle. For this is what Solomon said: "Free men will serve a wise servant" (Eccles. 10:28). This saying serves as a warning to Philemon, so that he would receive him at least for this reason, if he could not be moved by love.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "C" (stray mark) omitted; "sociam" read as "socium" (partner); "sc" as "se"; "lau- dat" as "laudat"; "Serto" as "Servo"; "bac" as "hac". The quotation corresponds to Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 10:28 (Vulgate 10:28/25), not Ecclesiastes; the author attributes it to Solomon. The passage is from the commentary usually transmitted under Ambrose's name (Ambrosiaster).
